svg.text: Threat intelligence: STIX 2.1, MITRE ATT&CK 20.1 and MITRE D3FEND 1.6.0 ontology

27 nodes · 16 relationships · 3 implied labels, generated from crosswalk.json, from the model.json of STIX 2.1, MITRE ATT&CK 20.1, MITRE D3FEND 1.6.0. The main arrows are named by their relationship type; hover any arrow for its name and description, and cards link to the term in its standard.
subtype: also carries the supertype's label

path.title: SAME_AS: stix:AttackPattern skos:narrowMatch attack:Technique. ATT&CK publishes its techniques and sub-techniques as STIX attack-pattern objects, keeping their STIX ids. A STIX attack pattern may come from elsewhere, e.g. CAPEC, so the ATT&CK technique is the narrower. Linked nodes share id and stixId, name.

SAME_AS: stix:IntrusionSet skos:narrowMatch attack:Group. ATT&CK publishes its groups as STIX intrusion-set objects. Any intrusion set a producer tracks is a STIX intrusion set, so the ATT&CK group is the narrower. Linked nodes share id and stixId, name.
SAME_AS: stix:Campaign skos:narrowMatch attack:Campaign. ATT&CK publishes its campaigns as STIX campaign objects. Linked nodes share id and stixId, name.
SAME_AS: stix:Malware skos:narrowMatch attack:Malware. ATT&CK publishes the malware among its software as STIX malware objects. Linked nodes share id and stixId, name.
SAME_AS: stix:Tool skos:narrowMatch attack:Tool. ATT&CK publishes the legitimate tools among its software as STIX tool objects. Linked nodes share id and stixId, name.

SAME_AS: stix:CourseOfAction skos:narrowMatch attack:Mitigation. ATT&CK publishes its mitigations as STIX course-of-action objects. A STIX course of action may be any action taken to prevent or respond to an attack, e.g. blocking a campaign's infrastructure, so the ATT&CK mitigation is the narrower. Linked nodes share id and stixId, name.

SAME_AS: attack:Technique skos:closeMatch d3fend:OffensiveTechnique. D3FEND imports ATT&CK's Enterprise techniques and sub-techniques as offensive technique classes, named by their ATT&CK ids. D3FEND's offensive techniques also include classes of its own grouping them by tactic, e.g. Initial Access Technique, and ATT&CK's Mobile and ICS techniques are other D3FEND classes. Linked nodes share attackId, name.
SAME_AS: attack:Technique skos:closeMatch d3fend:ATTACKICSTechnique. D3FEND imports ATT&CK's ICS techniques as classes of their own. Linked nodes share attackId, name.
SAME_AS: attack:Technique skos:closeMatch d3fend:ATTACKMobileTechnique. D3FEND imports ATT&CK's Mobile techniques as classes of their own. Linked nodes share attackId, name.

SAME_AS: attack:Tactic skos:closeMatch d3fend:OffensiveTactic. D3FEND imports ATT&CK's Enterprise tactics as offensive tactic classes, named by their ATT&CK ids, e.g. TA0001; the ATT&CK id is in the class IRI, not a property of its own, so the name joins them. Linked nodes share name.

SAME_AS: attack:Mitigation skos:narrowMatch d3fend:ATTACKEnterpriseMitigation. D3FEND imports ATT&CK's Enterprise mitigations, named by their ATT&CK ids, e.g. M1021, and relates each to the defensive techniques that implement it. ATT&CK's Mobile and ICS mitigations have no D3FEND counterpart, so the D3FEND class is the narrower. Linked nodes share name.

INSTANCE_OF: stix:File skos:relatedMatch d3fend:File. A STIX file is one observed file, with its name and hashes; a D3FEND file is a class of digital artifact, e.g. Executable File or Email Attachment, that offensive techniques produce and defensive techniques analyse. An observed file is an instance of the classes it belongs to.

INSTANCE_OF: stix:EmailMessage skos:relatedMatch d3fend:DigitalArtifact. A STIX email message is one observed message; D3FEND's Email is a class of digital artifact, and D3FEND's email filtering and analysis techniques act on its instances.
INSTANCE_OF: stix:Url skos:relatedMatch d3fend:DigitalArtifact. A STIX URL is one observed URL; D3FEND's URL is a class of digital artifact, analysed by URL Analysis.
INSTANCE_OF: stix:Process skos:relatedMatch d3fend:Process. A STIX process is one observed process; D3FEND's Process is a class of digital artifact.

INSTANCE_OF: stix:NetworkTraffic skos:relatedMatch d3fend:NetworkTraffic. A STIX network traffic object is one observed flow; D3FEND's network traffic classes, e.g. Outbound Internet Web Traffic, are the kinds of traffic its filtering and analysis techniques act on.
Every d3fend__File is also a d3fend__DigitalArtifact
Every d3fend__Process is also a d3fend__DigitalArtifact
Every d3fend__NetworkTraffic is also a d3fend__DigitalArtifact

g.title: stix__AttackPattern — Attack Patterns are a type of TTP that describe ways that adversaries attempt to compromise targets. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, aliases, name, description, kill_chain_phases

stix__Campaign — A Campaign is a grouping of adversary behavior that describes a set of malicious activities or attacks that occur over a period of time against a specific set of targets. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, name, description, aliases, first_seen, last_seen, objective

stix__CourseOfAction — A Course of Action is an action taken either to prevent an attack or to respond to an attack that is in progress. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, name, description

stix__IntrusionSet — An Intrusion Set is a grouped set of adversary behavior and resources with common properties that is believed to be orchestrated by a single organization. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, name, description, aliases, first_seen, last_seen, goals, resource_level, primary_motivation, secondary_motivations

stix__Malware — Malware is a type of TTP that is also known as malicious code and malicious software, refers to a program that is inserted into a system, usually covertly, with the intent of compromising the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of the victim's data, applications, or operating system (OS) or of otherwise annoying or disrupting the victim. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, aliases, first_seen, last_seen, architecture_execution_envs, implementation_languages, capabilities, malware_types, name, description, kill_chain_phases, is_family

stix__Tool — Tools are legitimate software that can be used by threat actors to perform attacks. Properties: id, type, spec_version, labels, created, modified, revoked, confidence, lang, external_references, granular_markings, extensions, aliases, tool_types, name, description, tool_version, kill_chain_phases

stix__EmailMessage — The Email Message Object represents an instance of an email message. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, date, content_type, message_id, subject, received_lines, additional_header_fields, is_multipart, body, body_multipart

stix__File — The File Object represents the properties of a file. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, hashes, size, name, name_enc, magic_number_hex, mime_type, ctime, mtime, atime

stix__NetworkTraffic — The Network Traffic Object represents arbitrary network traffic that originates from a source and is addressed to a destination. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, start, end, src_port, dst_port, protocols, src_byte_count, dst_byte_count, src_packets, dst_packets, ipfix, is_active

stix__Process — The Process Object represents common properties of an instance of a computer program as executed on an operating system. Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, is_hidden, pid, created_time, cwd, command_line, environment_variables
stix__Url — The URL Object represents the properties of a uniform resource locator (URL). Properties: id, type, spec_version, granular_markings, defanged, extensions, value

attack__Tactic — A tactic: the 'why' of an attack, the adversary's tactical objective, e.g. Stealth or Privilege Escalation. Techniques serve a tactic through the technique's kill chain phases. Holds 39 Tactic objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 15, Mobile 12, ICS 12. Examples: Initial Access, Execution, Persistence. Properties: stixId, attackId, shortname, name, description, url, created, modified, domains, version

attack__Technique — A technique: the 'how' of an attack, the means by which an adversary achieves a tactical objective. A sub-technique is a more specific technique, linked to its parent by SUBTECHNIQUE_OF. Holds 935 Technique objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 706, Mobile 125, ICS 104. Examples: Activate Firmware Update Mode, Monitor Process State, Automated Collection. Properties: stixId, attackId, platforms, isSubtechnique, impactType, remoteSupport, tacticType, name, description, url, created, modified, domains, version

attack__Campaign — A campaign: a grouping of intrusion activity conducted over a specific period of time against specific targets. Holds 61 Campaign objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 57, Mobile 3, ICS 10. Examples: Frankenstein, Night Dragon, CostaRicto. Properties: stixId, attackId, aliases, firstSeen, lastSeen, name, description, url, created, modified, domains, version

attack__Group — A group: a set of related intrusion activity that ATT&CK tracks by a common name, e.g. an APT or a criminal organisation. Holds 182 Group objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 178, Mobile 20, ICS 14. Examples: Axiom, Moafee, Cleaver. Properties: stixId, attackId, aliases, name, description, url, created, modified, domains, version

attack__Malware — Malware: a piece of software an adversary uses to compromise a system, e.g. a backdoor, ransomware or an implant. Holds 875 Malware objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 747, Mobile 127, ICS 25. Examples: Trojan.Mebromi, RIPTIDE, TinyZBot. Properties: stixId, attackId, aliases, platforms, isFamily, name, description, url, created, modified, domains, version

attack__Tool — A tool: a legitimate piece of software an adversary uses, e.g. a command-line utility, a remote access tool or a credential dumper. Holds 97 Tool objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 95, Mobile 2. Examples: Mimikatz, Windows Credential Editor, pwdump. Properties: stixId, attackId, aliases, platforms, name, description, url, created, modified, domains, version

attack__Mitigation — A mitigation: a security control that prevents a technique, or makes it harder, e.g. Multi-factor Authentication or Network Segmentation. Holds 109 Mitigation objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 44, Mobile 13, ICS 53. Examples: Authorization Enforcement, Access Management, Communication Authenticity. Properties: stixId, attackId, name, description, url, created, modified, domains, version

d3fend__OffensiveTactic — Per ATT&CK, these are defined as Tactical Goals, not Tactics per se. Many children also fit definition of tactics. Some are neither tactics or tactical goals really (e.g., Execution, which is a useful grouping, but an action, not really a tactic or technique. Holds the 65 D3FEND classes under OffensiveTactic in D3FEND 1.6.0, e.g. Impact, Stealth, Discovery. Properties: uri, framework, name, definition, d3fendId, attackId, capecId, kbArticle, synonyms, prefLabel, altLabels, comment, seeAlso, isDefinedBy, deprecated, displayOrder

d3fend__OffensiveTechnique — Holds the 875 D3FEND classes under OffensiveTechnique in D3FEND 1.6.0, e.g. At, DLL, DNS. Properties: uri, framework, name, definition, d3fendId, attackId, capecId, kbArticle, synonyms, prefLabel, altLabels, comment, seeAlso, isDefinedBy, deprecated, displayOrder

d3fend__ATTACKICSTechnique — Holds the 131 D3FEND classes under ATTACKICSTechnique in D3FEND 1.6.0, e.g. Wi-Fi - ATTACK ICS, ATTACK ICS Technique, Hooking - ATTACK ICS. Properties: uri, framework, name, definition, d3fendId, attackId, capecId, kbArticle, synonyms, prefLabel, altLabels, comment, seeAlso, isDefinedBy, deprecated, displayOrder

d3fend__ATTACKMobileTechnique — Holds the 179 D3FEND classes under ATTACKMobileTechnique in D3FEND 1.6.0, e.g. ATTACK Mobile Technique, Hooking - ATTACK Mobile, Accounts - ATTACK Mobile. Properties: uri, framework, name, definition, d3fendId, attackId, capecId, kbArticle, synonyms, prefLabel, altLabels, comment, seeAlso, isDefinedBy, deprecated, displayOrder

d3fend__DigitalArtifact — An information-bearing artifact (object) that is, or is encoded to be used with, a digital computer system. This concept is broad to include the literal instances of an artifact, or an implicit summarization of changes to or properties of other artifacts. Holds the 904 D3FEND classes under DigitalArtifact in D3FEND 1.6.0, e.g. Log, RAM, ROM. Properties: uri, name, definition, d3fendId, attackId, capecId, kbArticle, synonyms, prefLabel, altLabels, comment, seeAlso, isDefinedBy, deprecated, displayOrder

d3fend__File — A file maintained in computer-readable form. Holds the 64 D3FEND classes under File in D3FEND 1.6.0, e.g. File, Alias, Email. Properties: uri, name, definition, d3fendId, attackId, capecId, kbArticle, synonyms, prefLabel, altLabels, comment, seeAlso, isDefinedBy, deprecated, displayOrder

d3fend__Process — A process is an instance of a computer program that is being executed. It contains the program code and its current activity. Depending on the operating system (OS), a process may be made up of multiple threads of execution that execute instructions concurrently. A computer program is a passive collection of instructions, while a process is the actual execution of those instructions. Several processes may be associated with the same program; for example, opening up several instances of the same program often means more than one process is being executed. Holds the 26 D3FEND classes under Process in D3FEND 1.6.0, e.g. Process, DHCP Service, Mail Service. Properties: uri, name, definition, d3fendId, attackId, capecId, kbArticle, synonyms, prefLabel, altLabels, comment, seeAlso, isDefinedBy, deprecated, displayOrder

d3fend__NetworkTraffic — Network traffic or data traffic is the data, or alternatively the amount of data, moving across a network at a given point of time. Network data in computer networks is mostly encapsulated in network packets, which provide the load in the network. Holds the 38 D3FEND classes under NetworkTraffic in D3FEND 1.6.0, e.g. Network Traffic, OT Network Traffic, DNS Network Traffic. Properties: uri, name, definition, d3fendId, attackId, capecId, kbArticle, synonyms, prefLabel, altLabels, comment, seeAlso, isDefinedBy, deprecated, displayOrder

d3fend__ATTACKEnterpriseMitigation — Holds the 42 D3FEND individuals of the classes under ATTACKEnterpriseMitigation in D3FEND 1.6.0, e.g. Audit, Data Backup, Code Signing. D3FEND states that every ATTACKEnterpriseMitigation semantic-relation some DefensiveTechnique, which it links by related. Properties: uri, kind, framework, name, d3fendComment
